plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A bushy perennial cultivated for its dense, layered flower heads in a huge range of forms, from pompons to spiders. It is among the last major garden flowers to bloom in the Northern Hemisphere and tolerates light frosts.
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide, especially East Asia, Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums bloom in response to shortening days (short-day plants), and the flower is the emblem of Japan's Imperial family and is celebrated at Japan's Chrysanthemum Festival.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark leaves that bears slightly fragrant, open single or semi-double flowers. It blooms earlier than the common camellia and is a valuable source of color and nectar for pollinators in late autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (October to December)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan; widely grown in the southeastern United States, Mediterranean Europe and Australia
plants.funFact: Seeds of Camellia sasanqua are pressed to produce sasanqua oil, used in cooking, cosmetics and hair care in Japan.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large semi-deciduous tree that erupts in clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, often before the leaves fully emerge. In late spring in the Southern Hemisphere, streets lined with jacarandas become carpeted with fallen blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring (October to December in the Southern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia (Grafton, Sydney, Brisbane) and New Zealand's northern regions
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because of its roughly 70,000 jacaranda trees, and an old student superstition says a bloom falling on your head brings good luck in exams.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A tropical shrub native to Mexico whose showy colored bracts, not true petals, surround tiny yellow flower clusters called cyathia. In the wild it can reach several meters tall, while potted forms are a seasonal icon.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; grown outdoors in warm climates and indoors worldwide
plants.funFact: Poinsettias need long nights of about 12 hours or more for around 8 to 10 weeks to color their bracts, which is why they peak around late November and December.
